thread:
Alex W: hey team — opened PR https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/-/merge_requests/6218 that changes routing fallback order. Need runtime + infra + security eyes before I can schedule a canary. The change swaps cost-priority routing to prefer low-latency pools for small seqs.

Priya S: putting an async ask here — can someone from runtime take first pass? cc @Jordan R and @Sam I for infra bits.

Jordan R: I can take runtime review tomorrow morning. quick question: does this alter the kernel selection path or only routing policy?

Alex W: only routing policy surface — runtime kernel selection unchanged. but it will route some low-token requests to a different pool which may hit different quantized model builds.

Sam I: infra note: this new pool touches the kms-encrypted model cache path (s3 -> local cache with KMS double-wrap). @Mei L we'll need a quick review on the KMS usage and audit events. also, do we have capacity in eu-west for the canary?

Mei L: I can do a security skim. specifically check: (1) does the PR add new plaintext config anywhere? (2) any cross-account IAM changes? please paste the diff snip if possible.

Alex W: thanks — diff excerpt below:
```
- route_priority: [cost, latency]
+ route_priority: [latency, cost]
- model_pools: [general, low_latency]
+ model_pools: [low_latency, general]
```
No new plain text secrets. IAM unchanged. The cache path already uses KMS envelope keys.

Mei L: quick ack — looks fine from the config side. I want to confirm audit events are emitted for cache key unwraps; file an issue if not. otherwise :eyes: on the canary once scheduled.

Priya S: infra — can you confirm eu-west capacity? Sam?

Sam I: checked: we have 8 spare slots in the low_latency pool but autoscale is capped for that tenant. if canary is small (<=10qps) we're good. we should set a hard cap and a quick rollback policy.

Alex W: plan: schedule a 1-hour canary tomorrow 09:00-10:00 UTC, 5% traffic, hard token cap 50, auto-rollback on error rate >1.5%. who can own rollback?

Jordan R: I can be on-call for the canary rollback. will monitor latency and error rates.

Priya S: leaving a note to add a short runbook snippet in the PR describing rollback steps + who to ping.

deploy-bot: Canary window scheduled: 2026-03-19 09:00 UTC — owner: Jordan R — notif: #incidents if auto-rollback triggers.

Alex W: perfect. I'll add runbook, update PR, and request formal LGTM from runtime and security once done. thanks all :thumbsup:
